title: Station controls and receive tools
blurb: Choose the right receiver control for each interference problem and explain what ALC, tuner, TUNE and LOAD do.

G4A01.why: A notch filter cuts a **narrow slot** in the passband, removing a steady carrier while leaving the voice around it.
G4A01.trap: Splatter from adjacent signals and impulse noise need different tools (filters, blanker).

G4A02.why: Switching to the opposite sideband moves the passband to the other side of the signal, so a **nearby interferer may fall outside** it.
G4A02.trap: It doesn't remove impulse noise or add capacity.

G4A03.why: Impulse noise is brief, so the blanker **cuts receiver gain for just that instant**, then restores it.
G4A03.trap: It doesn't widen bandwidth or clip: it mutes the gain.

G4A04.why: Tuning the output circuit to resonance makes the tube deliver power to the load, so **plate current dips sharply**.
G4A04.trap: A peak is what you see in output power, not plate current.

G4A05.why: ALC senses overdrive and **turns the exciter down** so the amplifier isn't driven too hard.
G4A05.trap: ALC doesn't shape audio response, remove harmonics or raise efficiency.

G4A06.why: At the radio, a tuner makes the transmitter see a load it likes, so it can **deliver more power to the feed line**.
G4A06.trap: A tuner at the radio doesn't change SWR on the feed line itself.

G4A07.why: Noise reduction removes noise by processing the audio. Turn it up and **the wanted signal gets distorted** too.

G4A08.why: LOAD sets how much power is drawn off. Raise it until you get the **desired output, staying under maximum plate current**.
G4A08.trap: SWR on the antenna is for the tuner; LOAD works against plate current.

G4A09.why: The amplifier's relay needs time to **switch the antenna over**. Delaying RF keeps power from hot-switching the contacts.
G4A09.trap: Key clicks and overmodulation aren't what the delay is for.

G4A10.why: A keyer turns paddle presses into **automatically timed dots and dashes**.
G4A10.trap: T/R switching and antenna changeover are done by relays, not a keyer.

G4A11.why: Digital audio tones need clean, linear amplification. ALC action **distorts** the signal, so keep it inactive.

G4A12.why: Two VFOs hold two frequencies, so you can **transmit on one and listen on another**: split operation.
G4A12.trap: A transceiver can't send on two frequencies or transmit and receive simultaneously.

G4A13.why: An attenuator in front of the receiver reduces strong inputs so they **don't overload** it.
G4A13.trap: It acts on the receive path only, not on transmit power.
